# external.tpa__mntn_matched_taxonomy__v2

## Purpose
The DS19 ("MNTN Matched" / "MM Core") **keyword id -> name** dimension. Resolves a DS19
`data_source_category_id` (e.g. `905072`) to its human-readable product-category keyword
(`"Dog Beds"`). Produced by the **ShopperGraph URL-classification pipeline**: advertiser URLs are
classified via LLM/embedding into a product-category name + a DS19 category id, and this table is the
resulting flat namespace dumped to GCS parquet
(`gs://mntn-data-archive-prod/shopper_graph/mntn_matched_taxonomy_bq/*.parquet`).

**Reach for it** whenever you have raw DS19 category ids (from `ipdsc__v1` DS19 arrays,
`product_categorization`, or `targeted_signal`) and need the keyword names. This is the **only
BQ-queryable id->name source for DS19** — you cannot resolve DS19 names through
`integrationprod.categories` because DS19 ids collide with DS16 ("MNTN Taxonomy Data") in that table
(verified 2026-07-15, AUDI-1089).

## Grain & keys
- **Grain:** one row per `data_source_category_id` (DS19 keyword). Verified: 231,953 rows =
  231,953 distinct `data_source_category_id` (1:1, no dupes).
- **Key / join column:** `data_source_category_id`.
- **Single-DS table:** `data_source_id = 19` on every row — it is not a real dimension here, just a
  constant tag. This table is DS19-only.
- **Flat, not hierarchical:** despite the "taxonomy" name there is no tree. Every row has
  `is_leaf_node = TRUE` and `parent_id = 1` (the single ShopperGraph root). One root, all keywords as
  direct leaf children.

## Column meanings (only the non-obvious ones)
- **`data_source_id`** — always `19` (DS19 "MNTN Matched"). Constant, not a filter dimension.
- **`data_source_category_id`** — THE join key: the DS19 keyword id. Empirically spans **~100001 -
  979321** (231,953 ids). NOTE: the id space is **much broader than the old ">=900000" prose** — the
  >=900000 block is only 26,291 of the 231,953 ids; ~100,000 sit in 100000-199999 and ~105,000 in
  200000-899999. Do **not** filter to `>= 900000`.
- **`parent_id`** — always `1` (the ShopperGraph root node id). Flat namespace; carries no real
  hierarchy.
- **`partner_id`** — entirely **NULL** (0 populated). Unused.
- **`advertiser_id`** — entirely **NULL**. This is a global taxonomy, not per-advertiser.
- **`name`, `description`, `path`** — all three carry the **same** human-readable keyword string
  (e.g. `"Dog Beds"`, `"Electrolyte Supplements"`). Use `name`; the other two are redundant copies.
- **`names`** — a JSON **string** `{"names": ["ROOT", "ShopperGraph", "<keyword>"]}` (the readable
  path array). `names[1]` = `"ShopperGraph"` (the pipeline), `names[2]` = the keyword. Parse with
  `JSON_EXTRACT` / `JSON_EXTRACT_STRING_ARRAY`; do not raw-string-match.
- **`path_from_root`** — a JSON **string** `{"pathFromRoot": [0, 1, <data_source_category_id>]}` — the
  numeric-id path (0=ROOT, 1=ShopperGraph, then the leaf's own id). This is the numeric/struct format
  (mirrors the two-format `tpa.categories.path_from_root` gotcha); it is NOT a readable `"A > B > C"`
  breadcrumb here.
- **`is_leaf_node`** — always `TRUE` (every keyword is a leaf).
- **`navigation_only`** — always `FALSE`.
- **`deprecated`** — `TRUE` for only 2 of 231,953 rows. **`public`** — `TRUE` for all but 1 row.
- **`sort_order`** — effectively **NULL** (unused).
- **`created_date`, `updated_date`** — DATE (not epoch, not timestamps): row provenance in the
  taxonomy build. `created_date` ranges 2024-05-09 -> 2025-09-19; `updated_date` is NULL for most
  rows (max 2026-03-19). Use them for "when did this keyword enter the taxonomy", not as event times.

## Joins & relationships
- **`ipdsc__v1` (DS19 rows) -> this table.** `ipdsc__v1` is one row per `(ip, dt, data_source_id)`
  carrying an ARRAY of category ids; unnest the array and join
  `element = data_source_category_id`. Grain: **N ipdsc category-ids : 1 taxonomy row** (this side's
  key is unique, so the lookup adds no fan-out; ipdsc is the many side). Pattern:
  `... UNNEST(data_source_category_ids.list) e ... JOIN tax t ON t.data_source_category_id = e.element`
  with `ipdsc.data_source_id = 19`.
- **`product_categorization` / `targeted_signal` GCS parquet -> this table.** Same 1:1 lookup on the
  taxonomy side (DS19 id -> keyword name).
- **Do NOT join DS19 ids to `integrationprod.categories`** — DS19 ids share the id space with DS16
  there, so a join returns the wrong (DS16) names. This table is the correct DS19 resolver.

## Gotchas
- **Prose drift reconciled (id space):** the old `data_catalog`/`data_knowledge` note said this table
  "covers the >=900000 space." Live data shows the DS19 keyword id space is **~100001-979321**
  (231,953 ids); `>= 900000` captures only 26,291 of them (e.g. `100001 = "Job Searching"`,
  `900000 = "Electrolyte Supplements"`, `979321 = "Will Creation"`). Filtering to `>= 900000` silently
  drops ~89% of the keyword namespace.
- **Count drift (flag, unresolved):** the `data_knowledge` DS19 section says "~20,000 keywords." This
  taxonomy carries **231,953** ids — ~10x more. Likely the ~20K is the actively-targetable subset vs
  the full generated ShopperGraph namespace; not resolved here.
- **Flat, not a tree:** `parent_id` always `1`, `is_leaf_node` always `TRUE`. Do not expect
  multi-level hierarchy or write parent-walk logic.
- **Redundant name columns:** `name = description = path`; `names` and `path_from_root` are JSON
  strings, not plain text — parse them.
- **External snapshot, no dedup/soft-delete filters:** whatever is in the GCS parquet is what you get
  (no `deleted` / `is_test` columns). It is a current-state dump refreshed by overwriting the GCS
  objects — there is **no date partition**; `created_date`/`updated_date` are provenance, not
  partitions. `deprecated`/`public` are the only staleness flags (and both are near-uniform).

## Cost & partitioning notes
- **EXTERNAL federated parquet, flat glob** — backing =
  `gs://mntn-data-archive-prod/shopper_graph/mntn_matched_taxonomy_bq/*.parquet` (single directory, no
  `dt=`/hive partitioning). Therefore **no partition pruning is possible**; every query re-reads the
  parquet object set from GCS. There is no partition column to filter — `require_partition_filter =
  false`.
- **Dry-run cannot estimate cost for this table.** `bash .claude/scripts/bq_run.sh --dry_run` on
  `SELECT *` returns a **"0 bytes" lower bound** (BQ does not pre-estimate external GCS sources) — that
  is not a real cost figure. `bq show` reports `numBytes = 0` (external tables carry no BQ storage
  metadata), so `approx_logical_bytes` is left null and real on-GCS size is unknown from BQ.
- **The only cost lever is column selection.** The object is small (231,953 rows x 17 narrow columns),
  so a full scan is cheap in absolute terms, but you cannot prune rows. For the common id->name
  lookup, `SELECT data_source_category_id, name` reads far less parquet than `SELECT *`.
- No `deleted`/`is_test` filters exist (external snapshot).

## Example queries
```sql
-- id -> DS19 keyword name (the common lookup; only the two needed columns)
SELECT data_source_category_id, name
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.tpa__mntn_matched_taxonomy__v2`
WHERE data_source_category_id IN (905072, 922262);

-- resolve DS19 category names for IPs in ipdsc__v1 (single load-day)
SELECT DISTINCT t.data_source_category_id, t.name
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.ipdsc__v1` i, UNNEST(i.data_source_category_ids.list) e
JOIN `dw-main-bronze.external.tpa__mntn_matched_taxonomy__v2` t
  ON t.data_source_category_id = e.element
WHERE i.data_source_id = 19 AND i.dt = '2026-06-10';
```
